=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/scripts/dispatch_workflow.py: dispatch() line 147, main() lines 197-199 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When `_post_dispatch` raises `ReadError` (e.g. subprocess timeout at line 112-113 after the POST was sent but before the response arrived), the exception propagates through `dispatch()` uncaught and hits `main()`'s `ReadError` handler at line 197, which unconditionally prints dispatched: false and exits 2. GitHub may have already accepted the POST request by the time the client-side timeout fires, so retrying on dispatched: false can create a duplicate workflow run.
  WHY: A 60-second subprocess timeout on the gh api POST that fires between the request being accepted and the response being delivered — which is more likely on slow network connections or under GitHub API load — leaves the caller with dispatched: false and exit 2. If the stage session retries the dispatch, two identical workflow runs are created. The docstring contract (lines 34-36) says exit 2 with dispatched=true means never dispatch again, but exit 2 from _post_dispatch failure reports dispatched=false while the POST may have succeeded, violating that contract.
- .claude/scripts/dispatch_workflow.py: main() lines 197-199 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The ReadError catch in main() does not distinguish between a pre-dispatch failure (recent_run_ids or default-branch read, line 143-145) and a post-dispatch failure (_post_dispatch, line 147). Both get the same dispatched: false and exit 2 treatment, but only pre-dispatch failures are guaranteed to have created no run. The poll-failure path in dispatch() (lines 155-161) includes guidance to check gh run list before dispatching again, but the _post_dispatch-failure path through main() does not include that guidance.
  WHY: A caller that reads dispatched: false on exit 2 from a post-dispatch ReadError has no way to know they should check for a potentially-created run before retrying. The existing test (test_read_failure_before_the_post_reports_dispatched_false, test_dispatch_workflow.py lines 114-123) correctly expects dispatched: false for pre-dispatch failures, but no test covers the ambiguity when _post_dispatch raised after potentially sending the POST.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/scripts/dispatch_workflow.py: `_post_dispatch` at lines 98-118; the new try/except wrapper at lines 142-180 introduced by the LAST RUN DIFF | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The LAST RUN DIFF added an explicit rule (the comment "From here on the run exists (or will), so every failure reports `dispatched: true`: a caller must look for the run, never dispatch again.") and applied it to the polling loop by wrapping `find_new_run` in try/except and returning `dispatched: True` on `ReadError`/`KeyError`/`TypeError`. The same rule is NOT applied to `_post_dispatch` itself: when `subprocess.run` raises `TimeoutExpired` after 60 s, when `OSError` is raised, or when `proc.returncode != 0` (network error, 4xx/5xx response), `_post_dispatch` raises `check_in_status.ReadError`. That exception propagates to `main()`, which prints `{"dispatched": False, "error": "..."}` and exits 2. The error string contains no "before dispatching again" advice — it just says "dispatch of {workflow} failed: {detail}".
  WHY: GitHub may have accepted the POST and created the workflow run before the subprocess error. With `dispatched: False` and no guidance to check `gh run list`, a caller following the documented retry behaviour will dispatch again and create a duplicate run. The fix only enforces the rule from the point where `_post_dispatch` returns successfully, not during the POST itself, so the rule introduced by this commit is applied inconsistently between the POST phase and the polling phase. The minimax reviewer flagged this exact gap during pass 1 ("If `_post_dispatch` raises after GitHub may have accepted the POST, `main()` reports `dispatched: False` and the error does not advise checking for an existing run before retrying") and the LAST RUN DIFF did not address it.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- .claude/scripts/dispatch_workflow.py: `_post_dispatch()` lines 98-118, error message at line 113 | severity=NIT | confidence=3

  WHY: A 60-second subprocess timeout can occur after GitHub accepts the POST but before the response is received. The caller sees `dispatched: False` and the error message, but without guidance to check `gh run list`, may retry and create a duplicate run. The `dispatch()` function's timeout path (lines 172-177) correctly advises "check `gh run list --workflow={workflow}` before dispatching again", but the `_post_dispatch` failure path does not.
